chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: “I heard him saying:”

“A pregnant woman near term and a nursing woman with little milk are under no blame if they break their fast in the Month of Ramaḍān, because they are not able to fast. Each of them must give a mudd of food as charity for every day in which she breaks the fast, and they must make up every day they broke later.”

key_terms.الْحَامِلُ الْمُقْرِبُ: a pregnant woman who is near the time of delivery
key_terms.الْمُرْضِعُ الْقَلِيلَةُ اللَّبَنِ: a nursing woman whose milk is insufficient
key_terms.بِمُدٍّ مِنْ طَعَامٍ: with one mudd of food as charitable compensation
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: making up a missed fast afterward
key_terms.لَا حَرَجَ: there is no sin or blame

ai.seo_question: Can a pregnant or breastfeeding woman break her fast in Ramadan, and what must she do afterward?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a pregnant woman near delivery and a nursing woman with insufficient milk. It permits them to break the fast of Ramadan when fasting is too difficult, while requiring both fidyah in the form of a mudd of food for each missed day and later qada' of those days.
